governance_maturity.rationale: The governance framework demonstrates all characteristics of CMM Level 3 (Defined). Standardized processes exist and are documented for: defect tracking (DEFECT_LIBRARY.md with 32 entries using consistent schema), change management (REVISION_HISTORY.md with 177 entries), backup protocol (BACKUP_PROTOCOL.md), session startup (AGENTS.md §9), runtime governance (AGENTS.md §13 with T0/Tmid/Tend checkpoints), baseline verification (CURRENT_BASELINES.md), and quality standards (CAQS_v1.0.md). Processes are institutionalized across sessions — any operator following AGENTS.md can execute them. Level 2 (Managed) is achieved through session tracking, defect categorization, and basic metrics. Level 4 (Quantitatively Managed) is partially achieved (SHA-256 hashes, certified counts, quality scores) but inconsistent: SESSION_STATUS is stale, baseline verification is incomplete across sessions, and cross-document metrics are not automatically reconciled. Level 5 (Optimizing) is partially achieved through the defect library's learning loop (DL-019 led to backup protocol, DL-029 led to 8 prevention rules, DL-020 led to string-aware parsers) but improvement is reactive — triggered by discovered defects rather than proactive measurement. The governance guard itself has not been updated to incorporate its own learned lessons (still uses DL-029-vulnerable window scanning).
self_correcting_evidence: DL-019 (concurrent-write data loss) → BACKUP_PROTOCOL.md enacted with hard rules
DL-020 (validator brace-matcher undercount) → string-aware parser applied to extraction methods
DL-029 (regex block-scan false positives) → 8 permanent prevention rules codified in S802 findings
DL-022 (null-array crash) → Insertions 1+2 applied to app.js with independent verification
DEFECT_LIBRARY.md entries consistently include root cause analysis, detection rules, and regression tests — each defect generates reusable prevention
AGENTS.md §12 (No Staged Findings) was enacted after DL-019/DL-020 were lost in session reports without defect library entries
self_correcting_limitations: The governance guard plugin still uses the DL-029-vulnerable ±1200 char window method despite the project proving it produces ~75% false positives
CURRENT_BASELINES.md §3 still lists DL-008 as CRITICAL with 67 items — S802 resolved this but the document wasn't updated
Self-correction is reactive (triggered by defects) not proactive (triggered by metrics trending out of tolerance)
No automated cross-document consistency verification catches stale/contradictory information between CURRENT_BASELINES, SESSION_STATUS, and DEFECT_LIBRARY

summary: The CMA Part 1 Exam Simulator governance framework is well-architected, extensively documented, and demonstrates institutional learning from past failures. It scores 78/100 on maintainability, 82/100 on auditability, and 85/100 on repeatability. CMM Level 3 (Defined) is achieved — processes are standardized and documented. The framework is self-correcting in that defects produce lasting process improvements (BACKUP_PROTOCOL, prevention rules, string-aware parsers). However, CONDITIONALLY_READY status reflects three critical document-staleness issues: AGENTS.md contains stale certified counts, SESSION_STATUS has not been updated since 2026-07-24, and CURRENT_BASELINES.md §3 still reports DL-008 CRITICAL risks that S802 proved were 100% false positives. Additionally, the governance guard plugin itself uses a DL-029-vulnerable detection method — the framework's own lessons have not been applied to itself. With the 6 conditions above addressed, the framework would be READY for maintenance mode.
